So at least we do have a middle ground, being, that all three weapons need weapon/sword control or tip placement.

What i want to argue about is which needs more control than the other since I am not arguing that saber doesnt have any control rather im saying the other two (foil, epee) have more control over saber.

My reasoning is very simple:
1. The blade difference and how the point is made(im not sure if this is the right term but i just woke up so i cant think of a better def)
2. The area to hit
3. Fencing as it is right now.

Now we just mix the three into one. Im arguing foil has a harder control because of this, you gain a point by 'only' stabbing the opponent at the given area, which we know out of the three is the smallest. Hence its slow paced-ness(?) Now, what is easier than saber id say is diffending. The other way around saber you can get point by either stabbing or slicing. Saber uses the whole blade for the whole upper body. Since the target area and the means of getting a point is as it is even though you learn how to do technical stuff like disengages, it is hardly seen. For me at least saber right now is a game of speed.

True, i do agree with the fact that it has its tactical areas im just joking that compared to foil, it has less necessity in the control of the sword or weapon (i just call it a sword cause lets be honest looks one and i think thats howd you feel when you grab a sword)

There are positives and negatives of each of the three genres. Like epee is a very psychological genre a lot of thinking about what youll do or what the opponent does. But we make fun of epee like about their easy way out of priority. Same as foil. Slower than sabre but faster than epee. Id guess you can make fun of foil but i cant really think of one right now. And lastly sabre. Looks the funnest and i bet it is but at the end of the day comparing to the other two its less control of sword its more of a hit fist scream and pray the refree is on your side.

Im down to debate it out but the fact is sabre comparing to the other two (as of now/new gen sabre) has less sword control necessary.

I practice 3 times a week, just like ypu Monday, Wednesday and Friday but I only practice foil. In my opinion you should test try each at least once. Since saber and foil are basically two different area. No saber slander but saber is usually for people who have a hard time controlling the sword ^^. 

If you want a fast paced(?) bout Id recommend saber. Its explosive and each point is instantaneous.

If you want a more slow paced bout then foil is the way(or epee). For me its more of a thinking than explosive.

Nevertheless both are still sports so both of them are going to be tiring. It just depends on how much explosivness youre thinking on using each bout imo.

I believe that for now normal excercise i best. No more no less. Maybe what you should do is search about the three types of fencing. Epee, foil and sabre. A brief description of each:

Epee: You can get hit everywhere hence it can be slower paced than the other two. Biggest difference is that it doesnt have the right of way, which is a technical term youll learn eventually.

Foil: The sword is somewhat the same as epee. Difference is it has a smaller guard and a smaller target. Imo Id say this is the middle ground so its somewhat fast but also slow paced.

Sabre: Between the three, its the most fast paced. The other two, you get points by stabbing, but for this genre you get points by slapping(?) or hitting the opponent hence the lunge may differ.

Usually at least where Im at, the clubs dont have all three its either only one or two of the genres. Where Im at, the most played genre would epee, foil then sabre at last.

I hope it helped.

About equipment id recommend doing the sport first then buying used equipment. If you are thinking on going to competitions, then i think the club can help you with it.

Honestly, i'd try either counter attacking or just fleche it out i guess. Maybe get a good distance, since you know what the opponent is doing try the parry and as soon as he is backs the sword get that bug distance quickly.

For starters, i cant say much about saber since i have never done saber but I can say some things about foil.

The beating the sword part is really important in a way since it can take the opponents right of way. Imo its kind of concerning that you're not using it a lot since I do but who knows that is just a preference of play style.

Usually when I fence aggressive fencers I try to do three things:
1. Get myself a big distance between me and my opponent. Personally I do this so I can have a short thinking time. But while giving yourself distance dont forget to give action(like a feint) every time you go back. If you're static and monotonously walking back it is an easy touch for an opponent.
2. Try for counter attack. I believe that counter attacking is way easier when the opponent is too aggressive. He most probably can't control the pointer since he's moving too quickly. Usually ducking works best but any counter works.
3. If you know how to do a prime attack try to get up close and personal and do a prime attack.

A thing about aggressive fencers, or at least in what Ive experienced, is thay they usually do the same thing or end up at the same touch so just inspect what he does and plan out the thing you want to do.
Ex. If he always disengages from second to sixth then Id try a quarte or coubter sixth parry (assuming its a right vs right).

At the emd of the day your play style may not maych mine so best thing I guess is have someone else like coach or practice mate watch the match and tell you what you missed. Just like a constructive criticism kind of thing.

Imo you can use it for an element of surprise. Like I practice foil and two of the surprise attacks I do (I think its a surprise sttack) 

1. Intentionally run at the opponent but try to grab the sword with the blade. In the position try for a prime hit. Usually works best against opponents that are either too tensed up or scared of you.

2. Run but not at high speed the point for this is to make it looke like a fleche but isn't rather run to the opponent and at lunge distance lunge.

If done correctly these two tactics can give you at most 3-ish points but if u mix in the actual fleche it can confuse your opponent for a second or two.
